title: Veiled Watch
dek: Voraketh’s shore library and lighthouse, also called the Temple of Secrets. Its books, shared stores and expedition meetings belong to one physical history; later encounters beyond the Chains remain separate.

facts.Role: Lighthouse library; writing, shared resources and expedition meetings
facts.Architecture: Stone temple/library on the shore; complete floor plan unrecovered
facts.Temple of Secrets: Another recorded name for the temple/library in the Veiled Watch scenes
facts.Final expedition: Construct kills Anky and Alfred on 20 April 2026; Cerwin falls the following day

body:
The Veiled Watch is a lighthouse and library on Voraketh’s shore, used as a meeting place, writing room and shared store. Its temple is also called the Temple of Secrets in the recovered scenes. The building is observed; the scope of every protection Anky associates with it is a separate question.

A lighthouse with a library inside

The structure’s opening places it on the island’s edge. In the narrated formation, stone rises from the sand and the interior is dimly lit, with plain walls, a library of initially empty books and a central desk with ink. Later narration brings Pappy to the large lighthouse-like structure beside the water.

The site is called a temple within those scenes. Anky calls it the Temple of Secrets, and a later speaker inside the same writing setting uses that name too. The quest record subsequently identifies the Veiled Watch as the large stone library with a lighthouse. These overlapping descriptions establish the physical site behind the record context, while leaving a complete floor plan unrecovered.

Shared knowledge before another departure

Anky uses the temple for practical cooperation as well as writing. The wider March record includes an angel-made map and his wish that useful observations be shared. On the later arrival of supplies sent through Farkur, he sets out equipment with a note inviting companions to use and return it.

At the March gathering, Anky takes the company inside, shows a book and presents recording knowledge as a way to preserve what Voraketh might take from them. That is his explanation to the visitors. The writing materials and shared resources support a practical effort to preserve knowledge, while Anky’s expectations of protection remain his own explanation.

Duty amid personal loss

Anky says Voraketh is costing him things in his mind and that he wants to leave. He also reports that Nuru asked him for a full account, which he treats as a reason to remain. The record preserves his testimony and commitment without using them to prove the island’s entire metaphysics.

The meeting place and the expedition beyond it

The March quest begins with a company gathered after Anky has called them to hear about the Watch. Their discussion weighs reports about the Maw, magic and damage to the Chains. Cerwin claims to know a broken section and offers to lead them.

The party then leaves for that boundary. Narration follows their approach through the trees, with metallic movement heard ahead and scouts sent forward. The condition of the Chain is not established merely by the earlier argument at the library. Planning at the Watch and confronting the guardians are different stages at different places.

Departure and the recovered fatal encounter

In the April departure account, Anky sets aside a northern boat plan and proposes collecting motes as possible medicine for the goddess or tree. That is his hypothesis. He plans to use Portho’s Portal toward the furthest point he has reached, hoping to bypass guardians and suppressive conditions, and enters with Alfred Riverheart and Cerwin Rayolet.

The separate Wasteland scene supplies the fatal encounter. After escaping an earlier hostile creature, Anky and Alfred confront a different construct at the Binding Chains. Anky urges Alfred to flee; Alfred refuses to leave him. Explicit narration records the construct killing both on 20 April 2026 and throwing their bodies across the Chains. Cerwin falls the following day. Their later afterlife appearances follow these deaths; the mote theory is not established as a successful remedy.

Read Anky’s expedition and its recovered ending →

A proposed memory lead is not a completed test

In the later discussion with Murr, Ithilrûnë suggests checking whether the Watch might hold a record of memories the old wolf has lost. Murr is curious and sets off in that direction. The exchange records a proposal and movement toward it; it does not show a completed library test restoring her memory.

The quest then follows a wider search for former habitation. The company spends days traveling, finds a foundation whose substance crumbles when handled, and crosses toward a stream beyond the Chains. Those observations do not turn that ruined foundation or the later water-creature encounter into rooms of the Veiled Watch. Read Murr’s memory lead →

What later researchers inherit

Later researchers inherit a named library, records and a habit of comparing observations. Coralyn’s attention to how evidence is recorded and Ithilrûnë’s unresolved questions still matter. Neither a written claim nor a familiar meeting place settles every question about the Maw, the island’s history or a missing person.

The lighthouse and library can be placed on the shore. Their complete plan and the limits of the protections Anky describes remain unresolved.
